primary_work.title: Isolated Causal Effects of Natural Language

decision: NARROWED BEYOND IDENTIFIABLE ISOLATED LANGUAGE EFFECTS — NOT ADOPTED
rejected_claims: causal effects of natural-language interventions are unexplored
a significant or accurately estimated language-treatment effect identifies raw utterance equivalence
high-fidelity non-focal text adjustment identifies a latent intervention-target partition
focal-language shuffle sensitivity establishes joint causal grounding
remaining_rq: After conditioning on sufficient focal-treatment, non-focal-language, trajectory, interaction, and outcome statistics required by existing causal-effect and non-language CRL methods, can a preregistered external language law distinguish a concrete countermodel pair with identical isolated language effects but different raw-utterance equivalence and residual intervention-target partitions, and thereby strictly identify their joint refinement?
counterexample: Two models can share the same focal treatment extractor, sufficient non-focal text statistic, overlap, outcome law, interaction distribution, and isolated language effects while assigning different raw-utterance equivalence relations and latent target partitions.
